method: Complete pinned reads, Git/SHA256 verification, original AST callback execution using fake settings and a queued timer. No installation or GTK invocation.
findings: Settings on_view_enter connects changed each time without storing or disconnecting handler. Two original-method entries register two handlers in the control. Repeated live-view callbacks remain a source-level risk without actual GTK execution.

Reset reverts pending changes, queues a100ms reset and switches to previous view before callback. Original-method control records leave before reset:test-key and delay. Persistence semantics need real GSettings qualification; this is not proof of a persisted setting outcome.
Apply/revert is determined by save_settings on view leave; reset iterates every schema key including hidden ones. Unsupported variant types are silently skipped in UI construction.
Entry sorting uses order and widget object as tie-breaker, rather than key name. Equal order requires runtime widget comparability; no GTK failure claimed.
GUI build creates a wheel using selected Python and no build isolation; runtime data files/schema are installed separately. Source-only imports cannot prove installed resource availability.
Resource dependency output is split by whitespace. Build Python executable is interpolated without explicit quoting; paths containing spaces require separate validation.

Wheel uninstall uses distribution RECORD paths, legacy uninstall uses recorded paths, and prunes only empty directories; neither path was executed. Schema recompilation uses subprocess.call without propagating its exit status.
Delayed settings handlers and install/schema failure behavior are useful regression references, but no GPL source was copied into the library.

executed_control.scope: Original AST methods with fake settings and timer; no GTK or persistence runtime.

limits: 205/289 blobs reviewed; global full repository count150/500.
No GUI rendering, installation, uninstall or current performance measurement.
